message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm being AITA (Acting in a Terrible Way) in this situation with my mom and my flute. Let me break it down step by step. First, I know my mom and I don't have the best relationship. It's been tough since I moved in with my boyfriend, but things haven't really improved. I don't have all my stuff at her place because we're planning to move to Henderson in October. Right now, I only have essentials there. Today, I need to go to school to get pictures for the virtual graduation next month, and I want my flute with me. My flute is super important to me. I baby it a lot, don't let anyone touch it, not even experienced flute players. It's currently at my mom's house, and she knows I never want her to touch it, not even if it's in the case. This flute isn't just any old student model; it's an Azumi Atlus, a professional model. My mom likes to say she helped me get it. Well, when I was 17, I couldn't sign the contract at the music store on my own, so she signed for it in her name and set up the payment plan. However, I paid for it entirely. Within 10 months (on a 12-month plan), I paid off $2,316. It was my solid silver baby, and I finally owned it. Paying it off early even bumped my mom's credit score. But she thinks that because she helped me get it, she can touch it whenever she wants. Today, when she was picking me up, I told her I needed to grab my flute, which is hidden at her house in a safe spot. She said she could just bring it, but I firmly said no. Now, she won't stop calling and texting me, demanding to know where it is and saying, "I got it for you, I can touch it whenever I want." She thinks I'm disrespectful for not letting her touch my very delicate and expensive instrument. So, am I AITA? Let me think about this. On one hand, the flute is mine. I paid for it entirely, even though my mom signed the contract. I took responsibility to pay it off early, which shows maturity and dedication. I have the right to decide who touches my belongings, especially something as important and delicate as a professional flute. My mom's actions seem intrusive and disrespectful, especially since she knows how I feel about it. On the other hand, maybe she feels entitled because she was the one who signed the papers and helped me get it. She might not understand the emotional value I attach to it, thinking it's just an object. But I've made it clear that I don't want her to touch it, and she's ignoring that. I also need to consider the communication aspect. Did I handle the situation well? I told her no when she tried to bring it, but maybe I could have explained why it's important to me without being confrontational. However, she's the one who's persistent in contacting me, which might be adding to the stress. In terms of AITA, I don't think I'm acting terribly. I'm protecting my property and respecting my own boundaries. My mom's behavior is the issue here, not mine. I'm just asserting my right to control my belongings, which is reasonable.
